name: GLiDE
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear attention with full gated attention every 4th layer (16 of 64); partial RoPE
license: other (Fastino Community licence, LICENSE in repo)
notes: ADDED 2026-10-24. A DECISION model (task=decision), not a text generator: it takes a state (text, JSON, or text+image parts) plus typed questions - choice up to 255 options, noul, score - and returns a probability per option from a 255-way decision readout in ONE forward pass, zero output tokens. Full fine-tune of Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (board meta kind 'full fine-tune', base_model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, same 64-layer / 5120-hidden / 16-of-64-full-attention geometry as the base, so the architecture fields above are inherited unchanged from models/qwen3-8-27b). PARAMS: HF safetensors total 26,085,330,160 BF16 = 26.085B, which is BELOW the base's 27.781B. The card explains the gap - 51.2 GB language model + 0.92 GB vision encoder + 2.6 MB readout at bf16, 52.2 GB on disk - so the parameter set is not byte-identical to the base. The Decision Index board separately reports served_params 27.8e9 for this engine; the two figures disagree and both are recorded here rather than reconciled (26.085 is the safetensors count, 27.8B is what the board carries). active_params_b is left as the base's 27.781 (dense model, no MoE) and is NOT meaningful for a single-pass readout; flops_per_token_active is the tool's 6x active approximation and should be read with that caveat. EVIDENCE PROVENANCE: every benchmark row below is read from the upstream Decision Index board (huggingface.co/spaces/multimodalart/jev-decision-index, data/index.json, generated 2026-10-22T20:10:35Z), NOT from the self-reported row on the model card - the board lists glide-v1.2 with 'lab: false, jev: false', i.e. an entrant run under the shared harness, and all 110,201 requests completed. So vendor_claim is set false for these rows by the board's own attribution, even though the tool wrote them as card-sourced; the source id hf-fastino-glide is the card, and the board is the actual origin of the numbers. VERSION DRIFT - READ BEFORE COMPARING: this row is Decision Index 0.4.1 (headline 'full score' = balanced_skill = 60% private same-skill tests + 40% private new-domain tests, public benchmarks no longer count toward the rank). Everything in data/decision_index.jsonl is Decision Index 0.2.1, where the rank WAS the public chance-corrected index. The two indices are not on the same scale: under 0.4.1 GLiDE's public-only index is 71.99 and Cloudflare clef's is 61.71, whereas the 0.2.1 file holds clef at 61.21. GLiDE ranks #1 of 228 engines on 0.4.1 (rank_v 1, but rank_pub 5 - it is NOT first on the public-only index, Fastino's own GPT-class closed entrants sit above it there). The next three on 0.4.1 are Jeffan-31b-1710 69.75, baselabs mammoth-1 68.44 and Perplexity Decider v1.2 67.98. Against the catalog's 0.2.1-best self-reported GEV-26B-Decide (62.48) the gap is not interpretable, so no cross-version upset is claimed. SUB-SCORES: knowledge 60.59, language 75.49, retrieval 72.24, tools 88.04, artifacts 62.59 (skill-normalised, the five rows recorded below); tools is the strongest axis and artifacts the weakest. Latency median 92.9 ms per decision, p95 1,121.1 ms, mean 284 ms; ECE 0.0204 over 32 benchmarks and 110,201 requests - the best calibration on the board's top five and well under clef's 0.0395. HARDWARE: 52.2 GB BF16, needs one 80 GB GPU (tested on RTX PRO 6000 96 GB, B200, H100 80GB); 60.2 GB peak for a 39k-token question. That is NOT in this user's league - it fails the low-VRAM gate outright and is recorded as a reference point, not a runnable recommendation.

benchmarks.name: Decision Index 0.4.1 public index (balanced_raw)
benchmarks.config: Same row. balanced_raw = 100*sum_c(0.2*category[c]) over the 37 public benchmarks, chance-corrected per benchmark before averaging, coverage-adjusted so an unanswered request counts as wrong. This is the public-only index shown alongside the full score; it no longer counts toward the ranking.

benchmarks.name: Decision Index 0.4.1 breadth_skill
benchmarks.config: Same row. breadth_skill is the geometric-mean normalization of the same five category scores with a 0.1 shift: 100*(prod_c((0.1+0.9*c)^0.2)-0.1)/0.9. Rewards balance across areas rather than a single strong axis.
